reference.description: Reference should be a url, incident number, case ID, or other reference to the document the VERIS incident was based on.

summary.description:
Give a good descriptive summary of the incident in several sentences. Use natural language instead of VERIS notation, but we should be able to 'VERISize' the incident pretty well from just this description.
**REMINDER: IF THIS IS FOR THE DBIR AND NOT VCDB - DON'T RECORD VICTIM-INDENTIFYING INFO**

source_id.description: Source of the data (eg vcdb, vzir, hr dept)

campaign_id.description: (Way to associate multiple incident w/in one campaign).

incident.description: When did this incident initially occur?

compromise.description: How long from the first action to the first compromise of an attribute?

exfiltration.description: How long from initial compromise to first known data exfiltration?

discovery.description: How long from compromise until the incident was discovered by the victim organization?

containment.description: How long did it take the organization to contain the incident once it was discovered?

victim.description: More Info. **REMINDER - UNLESS THIS IS A VCDB INCIDENT, DON'T RECORD VICTIM-IDENTIFYING INFO IN ANY INCIDENT TO BE SUBMITTED TO THE DBIR**

employee_count.description: Number of employees.  Only use the count of the individual instance of a business (e.g. franchise location vs entire company) if the action vector was explicitly something unique to this individual instance. (i.e. This franchisee used a non-standard POS system that was then compromised.)

industry.description: Victim NAICS Code. You can look it up here or here.

government.description: The level of government if industry starts with 92.  Otherwise 'NA'

locations_affected.description: The number of victim locations, (stores, offices, etc), affected

region.description: The UN M.49 super-region and sub-region joined together. e.g. North America: 019021. South America (Brazil): 019005, Asia: 142000, East Asia (includes China): 142030, West Asia (Middle East): 142145, South Asia (India): 142034, Eastern Europe: 150151, Western Europe: 150155. Use 000000 if you do not know and 000001 for 'other' (includes international waters and outer space). If you only know the super-region, use zero's for the region. (e.g. 019000 for Americas.)

state.description: ALL CAPS. For US states, you can use the ISO_3166-2 2-character state code, otherwise use the full ISO_3166-2 Country subdivision code

notes.description: **UNLESS THIS IS FOR VCDB, DON'T RECORD VICTIM-INDENTIFYING INFO IF THIS WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE DBIR**

secondary.description: Secondary victims indicates that the breach being coded is the first part of a supply chain breach.

amount.definition: The number of known secondary victims. Should always be a positive number if victim_id is filled in.  May not represent all victims if some are unknown.

victim_id.description: List any secondary victims here.  IF a NAICS is known, list the NAICS code after a semi-colon.  For example: `verizon;517911`.  If only the NAICS code is known, list it first.  `;517911`

revenue.description: For the DBIR, this is a low priority field and is OK to not fill in.

malware.description: Think things a program does (rather than a person on a keyboard) More Info

unknown.description: If the actor is unknown, you *must* add a note of some type, otherwise the incident will not validate.

asset.description: What assets were affected by the incident actions. Data types and record count will be covered in the attributes section. More Info

variety.description: What varieties of assets were compromised?

amount.description: How many total systems were compromised?

ownership.description: Who owns the affected asset? This can allow us to identify employee-owned (BYOD) assets.

cloud.description: Only answer if you know for sure if the asset was hosted in a cloud service.

hosting.description: Where is the affected asset hosted/located?

management.description: Independent of physical location, who administers and maintains the affected asset?

role.description: Is the asset Information Technology (IT) such as email or the domain controller or Operational Technology (OT) such as rail-switching computers for a railroad or manufacturing robots for a manufacturing company.

attribute.description: What attributes were compromised? More Info

confidentiality.description: Was data (potentially) disclosed to an unauthorized party? More Info

data_disclosure.description: Was data disclosed?  This is the core determiner if this incident is a breach.  If this is 'Yes', it will be considered a breach.  If it is anything else, it will only be an incident.

data_volume.description: Amount of data breached in volume (GB)

data.description: Varieties (and amount) of data compromised. Click the red ‘Add’ button to record multiple data varieties.

integrity.description: Was a person manipulated or the state of a system changed? More Info

availability.description: Was something rendered partially or wholly unavailable? More Info

duration.description: Specific value of the specific selected unit, (i.e., # of 'days').

result.description: The result of the action.  If there's a difference between action result and actor intent, use the result not intent.

targeted.description:
Was this a targeted or opportunistic attack? More Info
N/A: Not an attack (e.g., unintentional actions)
Opportunistic: Victim was NOT pre-selected as a target; they were identified/attacked because they exhibited a weakness the attacker knew how to exploit.
Targeted: The victim is pre-selected as a target; the attacker(s) then determined what weaknesses exist within the target that could be exploited.

discovery_method.description: What discovery method was involved? More Info

internal.description: Discovered by entity within the victim organization.

partner.description: Discovered by a partner of the victim.

discovery_notes.description: How was the incident discovered? More Info

value_chain.description: Capabilities and investments an attacker must acquire prior to the actions on target, (either by purchase or investment in creating).  May be internal to the actors organization (vertically integrated org), or external (purchased in a criminal market).

development.description: Software that must be developed to accomplish the actions on target.

non-distribution services.description: Services provided and used by malicious actors other than those used for distribution of actor content

targeting.description: Things that identify exploitable opportunities.  These overlap heavily with data varieties that are compromised.

distribution.description: Services used to distribute actor content.

cash-out.description: Methods for converting something (likely the attribute compromised) into currency.

money laundering.description: Methods for concealing the origins of illegally obtained money.

impact.description:
Impact Info
**REMINDER - UNLESS THIS IS FOR VCDB, DON'T RECORD VICTIM-INDENTIFYING INFO IF SUBMITTING TO THE DBIR**
**Tip: Hold CTRL or COMMAND to select multiple items from a list.

iso_currency_code.description: ISO4217 currency code. More Info

overall_amount.description: The total amount lost in the given ISO currency code.

overall_min_amount.description: When 'overall_amount' would be a range, use this field for the minimum of that range. Note: Values here will not appear in searches for 'overall_amount'.

overall_max_amount.description: When 'overall_amount' would be a range, use this field for the maximum of that range. Note: Values here will not appear in searches for 'overall_amount'.

loss.description: Were any losses or costs reported for this incident? (Definitions for loss varieties and ratings are here)

plus.description: Plus is the appropriate place to extend the VERIS schema for your own needs.  Add organization-specific enumerations here.

master_id.description: Master_id is a type 4 UUID and is unique for every record (incident).

data_abuse.description: The data was used for fraud, used mischievously, used maliciously, or otherwise abused.

extra.description: Extra is a reserved name and should not appear in any objects. It should only be used for temporary derived columns during analysis.

corrective_action.description:
What corrective action(s) are planned (or recommended) to prevent and/or detect similar incidents in the future?
This can include general recommendations, specific changes to policy, procedures, personnel, and technology, short-term and long-term strategies, etc. Don't simply copy what the investigator said. Tie to the root causes listed above, and focus on practical, effective corrective actions.

control_failure.description:
What were the root control failures or weaknesses that allowed this incident to occur?
Obviously, there may be a multitude of factors that could be listed here. Include as many as you want, but focus on the issues most pertinent to why the incident occurred.

schema_version.description: Schema version in use. This should be 1.4.0 for this schema.

schema_name.description: Name of Schema.  This can be used to signal to software reading the schema which it is.  Common values are 'verisc', 'dbir', and 'vcdb'.

security_incident.False positive: False positive (response triggered, but no incident)

unit.NA: Compromise does not apply in the context of the security event.
Exfiltration does not apply in the context of the security event.
Discovery does not apply in the context of the security event.
Containment does not apply in the context of the security event.

variety.Backdoor: Hacking action that creates a backdoor for use.
variety.Brute force: Brute force or password guessing attacks.
variety.CSRF: Cross-site request forgery. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Disable controls: Disable or interfere with security controls
variety.Evade Defenses: Modification of the action (rather than the system, as in 'Disable controls') to avoid detection.
variety.Exploit misconfig: Exploit a misconfiguration (vs vuln or weakness)
variety.Exploit vuln: Exploit vulnerability in code (vs misconfig or weakness). This can be used with other hacking enumerations, (such as XSS when an XSS vuln exists.). Parent of many hacking varieties.
variety.Forced browsing: Forced browsing or predictable resource location. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Format string attack: Format string attack. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Hijack: To assume control over and steal functionality for an illicit purpose (e.g. Hijacking phone number intercept SMS verification codes)
variety.HTTP request smuggling: HTTP request smuggling. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.HTTP request splitting: HTTP request splitting. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.HTTP response smuggling: HTTP response smuggling. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.HTTP response splitting: HTTP response splitting. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Insecure deserialization: iterating over sequential or obvious values. https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Top_10-2017_A8-Insecure_Deserialization. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Mail command injection: Mail command injection. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Null byte injection: Null byte injection. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Offline cracking: Offline password or key cracking (e.g., rainbow tables, Hashcat, JtR)
variety.Profile host: Enumerating the state of the current host
variety.Prompt injection: Crafting malicious or misleading prompts to bypassing safety filters and executing unintended instructions in LLMs
variety.RFI: Remote file inclusion. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Scan network: Enumerating the state of the network
variety.Session prediction: Credential or session prediction. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Soap array abuse: Soap array abuse. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.Special element injection: Special element injection. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.URL redirector abuse: URL redirector abuse. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.

variety.Virtual machine escape: Virtual machine escape. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.XML attribute blowup: XML attribute blowup. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.XML entity expansion: XML entity expansion. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
variety.XML external entities: XML external entities. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.

cloud.NA: (cloud.No) Cloud is not applicable to this incident. Only use if computer's weren't involved (people, media, etc). Do not use for Desktops or other user assets.

hosting.External - unknown environment: A third party provided hosted the affected asset, but it is unknown whether the victim organization’s environment was shared or dedicated.
hosting.External - dedicated environment: A third party provider hosted the affected asset on servers dedicated to the victim organization.
hosting.External - shared environment: A third party provider hosted the affected asset on a shared physical device. This is common in web hosting services where multiple organizations’ web applications are resident on the same physical server.
hosting.Internal: The affected asset was hosted within the victim organization’s location.
hosting.NA: Hosting label is not applicable, a Human asset that clicks a malicious attachment is a common example as is portable assets like laptops or paper documents.
hosting.Other: Hosting arrangement known but not listed
hosting.Unknown: The hosting arrangement of the asset was not known to the incident responder or not recorded.

management.External: The affected asset was managed and maintained by a third party service provider or business partner.
management.Internal: The affected asset was managed and maintained by employees of the victim organization.
management.Co-managed: The affected asset was managed and maintained by both internal administrators as well as a third party provider or partner. There is a level of shared responsibility.
management.NA: Management label is not applicable, a Human asset that clicks a malicious attachment is a common example.
management.Unknown: The responsibility for management and maintenance of the affected asset was not known to the incident responder or not recorded.

role.Other: Known but not IT or OT
role.NA: The concept of a role is not applicable to the asset.

country.GS: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

variety.API key: Application Programing Interface key are used for programmatic access to applications, if unsure, use Credentials
variety.Credentials: Authentication credentials, such as username and password
variety.Internal: Sensitive internal data (e.g., plans, reports, emails)
variety.Multi-factor credential: Any additional authentication methods, aside from Username and password (e.g., OTP, biometrics)
variety.Payment: Payment card data (e.g., PAN, PIN, CVV2, Expiration)
variety.Personal: Personal or identifying information (e.g., addr, Email address, credit score)
variety.Sensitive Personal: Data which impacts a person's livelihood, quality of life, and ability to participate in daily activities such as SSNs or other National ID
variety.Session key: Session keys associated with an existing connection and used to identify the client, if unsure, use Credentials
variety.System: System information (e.g., config info, open services)

data_victim.Victim organization: The data was that of the victim organization rather than a customer, employee, etc.

state.Stored: Stored (either encrypted, unencrypted, or where encryption is unknown.
state.Other: Data state known but not listed.

variety.Misrepresentation: compromise of authenticity (e.g. masquerading as the legitimate owner of an account)
variety.Modify authentication: Modified how a user account is authenticated, such as removing MFA device
variety.Register MFA device: Register an attacker controlled MFA device to an account
variety.Software installation: On-disk software installation or code modification

targeted.Opportunistic: Opportunistic: victim attacked because they exhibited a weakness the actor knew how to exploit
targeted.Targeted: Targeted: victim chosen as target then actor determined what weaknesses could be exploited
targeted.NA: Not applicable.  Use when actor does not have a practical choice of targets or no intent (i.e. Error).

variety.Actor disclosure: disclosed by threat agent (e.g., public brag, private blackmail)
variety.Customer: reported by customer or partner affected by the incident
variety.Law enforcement: notified by law enforcement or government agency
variety.Security researcher: security researcher attempting to identify insecure data
variety.Unrelated 3rd party: Discovered by person unaffiliated with victim or threat actor
variety.Other: Discovery method was external and known but not listed including related 3rd parties

variety.Break in discovered: employee discovered evidence of a break in
variety.Hids: host IDS or file integrity monitoring
variety.Incident response: discovered while responding to another (separate) incident
variety.Infrastructure monitoring: Health and welfare monitoring of assets such as utilization, uptime, and SNMP alerts
variety.It review: Any routine maintenance, testing or review of it assets. (Includes inspect of assets, vulnerability scans, etc.)
variety.Offboarding: Use when the incident is discovered during the exit interview or offboarding/decommissioning of an employee.
variety.Reported by employee: reported by employee who saw something odd
variety.Other: Discovery method was internal and known but not listed

variety.Antivirus: Notified by antivirus company but not through AV product
variety.Audit: Audit performed by a partner organization
variety.Other: Discovery method was partner and known but not listed

variety.Bot: A small program that can be distributed, installed, and controlled en mass.
variety.Email: Develop an email such as for phishing.
variety.Exploit: Code to exploit a vulnerability, including web injects.
variety.Exploit Kits: Code sets capable of selecting and trying multiple exploits against a target.
variety.Payload: The portion a program that causes a negative effect.
variety.Persona: A fake representation of a person, such as fake social media profiles
variety.Physical: Development of something physical such as a skimming device
variety.Trojan: A program which masquerades as another program to get a target to execute malicious content
variety.Website: Development of any full website controlled by the attacker
variety.NA: No type of development was necessary
variety.Other: The variety of development required is known, but is not listed.
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of development investment other than it was present.

variety.C2: Command and control. Separate from distribution of mawlare or bots, this is how they are maintained
variety.Counter AV: Services for testing if malware is detected by anti-virus
variety.Escrow: Something kept in the custody of a third party until a condition has been fulfilled.
variety.Hashcracking: i.e. converting hashes into the text that produce them
variety.Marketplace: Use of a marketplace was required as part of this incident.
variety.Proxy: A proxy service (either formally or informally hosted) is used by the actor to obscure their source
variety.VPN: A VPN service (either formally or informally hosted) is used by the actor to obscure their source
variety.NA: No type of non-distribution service was necessary
variety.Other: The variety of non-distribution service required is known, but is not listed
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of non-distribution service investment other than it was present.

variety.Lost or stolen credentials: lost or stolen credentials, including credental stuffing, used to pick an organization as a target
variety.Misconfigurations: Knowledge of system misconfigurations used to pick an organization as a target
variety.Partner: The actor used access to a partner to target the victim.
variety.Personal Information: Information on individuals such as title, interests, physical location, etc, used to pick an organization as a target
variety.Physical: Targeting through physical means such as geographic location.
variety.Organizational Information: Information on an organization such as org chart, technologies in use, financial assets, etc, used to pick them as a target
variety.Vulnerabilities: Knowledge of software vulnerabilities, both at an organization or associated with a specific vendor's product, used to pick them as a target.
variety.Weaknesses: Knowledge of weaknesses other than vulnerability and misconfigurations used to pick an organization as a target
variety.NA: No type of targeting was necessary. (This includes targeted.Targeted since the victim was chosen without targeting.
variety.Other: The variety of targeting was known, but is not listed
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of targeting investment other than it was present.

variety.Botnet: For content distributed from a collection of bots.
variety.Compromised server: malicious content added to a benign server, such as a webserver, by the actor, without the permission or necessarily knowledge of the server’s owner
variety.Direct: Distributed directly from the actor's computer
variety.Email: Distribution by email including anonymous/one time and spam
variety.Partner: The actor distributed the attack to the victim through a partner.  (Indicates supply chain breach.)
variety.Phone: Distribution over the Plain Old Telephone System (POTS).
variety.Website: Malicious content shared intentionally, including bullet-proof hosting
variety.NA: No type of distribution was necessary
variety.Other: The variety of distribution was known, but is not listed
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of distribution investment other than it was present.

variety.Hijacked rewards: Recieve value meant for someone else, (such as redirected affiliate proceeds or click fraud
variety.Provide service: See distribution and non-distribution services for potential examples
variety.Sell stolen goods: likely the data.variety for breaches or asset for stolen assets
variety.Purchase stolen goods: Purchase physical goods as a means of transferring a compromised account's content or currency to the actor.
variety.NA: No type of cash-out was necessary
variety.Other: The variety of cash-out was known, but is not listed
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of cash-out investment other than it was present.

variety.Company: Trade-based, shell companies, under/over paying, cash-intensive businesses, etc, used for money laundering
variety.Cryptocurrency tumbling: Breaking an amount of cryptocurrency into smaller amounts and quickly filtering it through multiple accounts
variety.Employment: An individual believes they are legitimately employed, and launders money/items during the course of their employment.
variety.Gambling: Gambling related money laundering. (e.g. Converting to chips and back or big wins and losses.
variety.Provide service: See distribution and non-distribution services for potential examples
variety.Re-shipping: Individuals receive packages purchased through fraudulent means and subsequently repackage the merchandise for shipment, usually abroad.
variety.Smurfing: Breaking non-crypt currency up into smaller amounts to transfer
variety.Sell stolen goods: likely paired with value_chain.cash-out.variety.Purchase stolen goods
variety.NA: No type of money laundering was necessary
variety.Other: The variety of money laundering was known, but is not listed
variety.Unknown: Nothing is known about the need for or type of money laundering other than it was present.

variety.Asset and fraud: Asset (including physical currency) and fraud-related losses
variety.Other: Impact variety known but not listed.

overall_rating.Catastrophic: Catastrophic: A business-ending event (don't choose this if the victim will continue operations)
overall_rating.Damaging: Damaging: Real and serious effect on the "bottom line" and/or long-term ability to generate revenue
overall_rating.Painful: Painful: Moderate "hard costs", and impact felt through having to deal with the incident rather than conducting normal duties has quantifiable indirect costs
overall_rating.Distracting: Distracting: Limited "hard costs", but impact felt through having to deal with the incident rather than conducting normal duties
overall_rating.Insignificant: Insignificant: Impact absorbed by normal activities

data_abuse.Yes - Data ransomed: Data was ransomed by the threat actor, child of Yes
data_abuse.Yes - Identity theft: The data was used stealing individuals identity, child of Yes
data_abuse.Yes - Financial fraud: The data was directly used for financial fraud (ie using stolen payment cards), child of Yes
data_abuse.Yes - Posted on personal forum: The data was posted on a personal blog post or social media, child of Yes
data_abuse.No: Data was not misused or abused
data_abuse.Other: Neither 'yes' nor 'no' describes data abuse in this case.
data_abuse.Unknown: No information is known about if the data was abused
